pending.body: In overview.rs, the NH3 label reads `NH3-N {:.4} mg N/L` while in chemistry.rs it reads `Free NH3-N {:.5} mg NH3-N/L`. The unit suffixes differ: overview says 'mg N/L' (element basis) while chemistry says 'mg NH3-N/L' (which is the same thing but uses a different notation). Both are technically correct for the same quantity, but the inconsistency may confuse users comparing the two screens. Standardize on one label — either 'mg N/L' or 'mg NH3-N/L' — across both screens.

`crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:11-23,26-45` introduces legacy field mappings but does not apply them during `TankSnapshot` deserialization. Compatibility for renamed chemistry keys currently lives only in `crates/tank_tui/src/api_client.rs:119-145`, so any other Rust consumer that deserializes legacy `/snapshot` or `/load` payloads directly into `tank_core::TankSnapshot` will still fail with missing `*_mg_n_per_l` / `*_mg_p_per_l` fields. Move the compatibility into `tank_core` itself (for example with `#[serde(alias = ...)]` or a shared normalizer) instead of making each client reimplement the shim.

`crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:87-111` now computes TDS/conductivity from a fresh carbonate solve, but the public state helpers still read the cached `water.bicarbonate_mg_total` via `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:207-240` and `crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:317-322`. The new test at `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:256-289` explicitly asserts that snapshot values can exceed the cached helper values. That leaves two public APIs able to report different TDS/conductivity for the same `TankState`, which is a correctness/maintenance trap for any internal caller that does not go through `TankSnapshot`. Factor the fresh carbonate projection into a single shared helper or refresh the cache before every public accessor.
